body:
Agent99 --

I'll leave your ad hominem attacks to another thread, where they will be
treated as only more evidence that Peter and Woody were right, that you and
Pyro really don't like women! Very interesting stuff you are giving us to
analyse your psychology. Thanks!

On the argument, once again, you did not put up much in the way of one. So,
this will be brief.

Regarding the letter to Dr. Tyler, you agreed that TK's questions were
important. You ignored the fact that a.f.u. had been a discussion center for
those questions for a long time, and instead insisted that I and others
believed that TK was PC and a leftist. I don't recall any postings like that.
So much for your powers of observation.

In any case, call the members of this group what you will, since you will as we
are not in your nazi club, but think about it -- why was the opinion of this
psychologist (whom you would label a leftist) so important to TK?

On censorship, if stating a fact about Echelon troubles you, perhaps you would
feel happier if we didn't tell you about what's going on in the world. Guys,
keep that in mind, Agent gets upset if we tell him what's going on in real life
outside of the nazi theme park.

I find it interesting that Agent and Pyro are only willing to discuss what they
have put forth, and see no merit in other discussions. Are you two the group
censors? Regulars here at a.f.u. have had many factual discussions before
either of your arrivals. I don't consider the Protocols of the Elders of Zion
factual, but if you do, perhaps a less savvy newsgroup is where you belong.

As far as TK mentioning political rightists, well, no he may not have, as you
call it, though he did call the conservatives fools, but the definition of the
psychological type is still there. I believe that TK is no friend of the right
wing any more than he is of the left. That's how his friend and supporter John
Zerzan defines anarchy and TK has described himself as an anarchist. But do
also see Scott's earlier post on Hoffer and Adorno for more clarification.
Jumangi also had an interesting post a while back mapping out viewpoints in
quadrants. Sorry that you are so unforgivingly linear, or I would explain to
you some other things that have been brought up here on the topic.

Agent still hasn't answered my question on the leftist anti-tech movement in
the 1960's. I am really wondering more and more about this. Note that I did not
say that TK was part of this group, only that he witnessed that it did not
work. I am also wondering how influential Ellul was to this movement, and when
did TK first read Ellul?

As far as Agent's easy dismissal of the quote from ISAIF, paragraph 192, "Our
real enemy is the industrial-technological system, and in the struggle against
the system, ethnic distinctions are of no importance," I don't think that any
true-believing nazi sympathizer would agree with this and certainly would not
write it. It could have been left out, without causing much commotion, if he
didn't mean it. I think that TK really meant this, and consider that he carried
on a correspondence with one of those "disgusting hispanics" as Pyro would say,
for a number of years, counting Juan Sanchez Arreola as one of his few friends.

Concerning the Abraham Lincoln quote, there was an interesting PBS or such
special a year or so ago on the Lincoln-Douglas debates, and yes, the type of
thing you cited was discussed. I am no Lincoln expert, but Ellis is, and I
shall ask her about it. We all should, her presence here is sorely missed.

Agent, think for a minute about what you are trying to do. You are trying to
speak for TK, without really understanding what he is about, when in fact, you
are not concerned about the issues of ISAIF at all, and are only pushing your
personal nazi agenda. What would Ted think of your corruption of his ideology?

-Susan
